body:
I need drafted dialogue for seven short camp scenes in a single-player D&D Curse of Strahd game. Plain text only (no JSON, no markdown tables), nodes under `~ name`, one line per row as `Speaker [mood]: Text`, party option rows as `* option text -> node_name`, ASCII only (straight quotes and apostrophes, no accents or fancy dashes, no em-dash: use a comma or a full stop), 1-2 sentences a line, nothing over about 28 words, no placeholders like {name}. Finish without sending messages to anyone else.

## The situation

Ireena Kolyana (a proud, red-haired young woman in her early twenties, the dead burgomaster Kolyan's adopted daughter, found on a road as a girl with no memory of where she came from, twice bitten by the vampire lord Strahd) travels with the player's party. When the party makes camp and rests for the night, she sometimes asks for a word by the fire: a short scene, played once. She sits at the fire with the company. In this game she does not fight: something in the valley goes round her like water round a stone, so enemies do not touch her and she does not strike, and she hates standing back from fights while the others bleed.

Each scene has this shape:
- a node named for the scene: Narrator x1 (what the fire and she look like, one or two sentences), then Ireena x2 (her opening), then two party option rows (the party is a group of adventurers; the option text is what the player's character says, first person, short, under 14 words, no skill checks);
- two reply nodes, named `<scene>_a` and `<scene>_b`, each Ireena x1 or x2, one for each option. The scene ends after the reply (do not write `-> END`, I will).
That is about 7 lines and 2 option rows per scene: 7 scenes = about 49 lines.

## The seven scenes (the name is the node name; the note says when it is offered and what it is about)

1. kept_back: offered once the party has been through many fights with her at the side. Ireena is restless: she has watched every fight from behind the line and cannot answer a single blow. She does not want to be a thing the valley is keeping. She asks for sword practice by the fire, her hands steady, and means it. Options: one takes her seriously (practice at dawn), one tells her it keeps her alive.
2. burial: offered after her father's burial. Ireena is formal and exact about the funeral, as she gets when she grieves: how the grave beside her mother was dug, the lamp she carried, who spoke. She asks whether the party remembers the words as they were said, because she wants them kept exactly. Options: one repeats that Kolyan was well sent off, one admits they remember little but remember that she did not look away.
3. window: offered after Strahd came to her window and she was saved from going. She says she does not want to be watched asleep, and asks that someone near her stays awake. She is ashamed that she wanted to go. Options: one promises to take the watch before hers, one tells her honestly they cannot promise to stop it every time.
4. izek: offered after the party told Izek, the Baron's enforcer in Vallaki, that Ireena is the sister he lost in the woods as a boy. Ireena turns it over: she has a brother she does not remember, a big, scarred man who carved her face into dolls. She does not know what a sister owes him. Options: one says she owes him nothing yet, one says he is a man who has been looking for her all his life.
5. pool: offered after the Pool of the White Sun in Krezk, where she saw a dead man in the water who knew her by another name. TWO opening variants: pool_promised (she promised him she will come back to the pool when the devil is dead) and pool_stayed (she chose her own life and said goodbye to him). Use the node names `pool_promised` and `pool_stayed` for the two openings (each Narrator x1, Ireena x2), both with the same two option rows pointing to the same `pool_a` and `pool_b` replies (so the replies must read right after either opening). Options: one asks what he looked like, one says it is her choice either way.
6. amber: offered after a member of the party has taken a gift from the Amber Temple in the northern mountains, a temple of old bargains sealed in amber. She says she can smell old resin on them, sweet and wrong, and it frightens her more than anything the devil has done, because he takes and these were given. She does not forgive easily. Options: one tells her what it cost, one tells her it was worth it.
7. castle_eve: offered the night before the party goes to Castle Ravenloft, the devil's home, where she has never been and knows where the stairs go. She is calm and formal. She says what she wants done if she is taken: no rescue from the party at the price of the party, and a message for her brother Ismark. Options: one refuses to leave her, one promises the message will be delivered.

## Voice reminders

IREENA: direct and proud; short sentences, no ornament; dry humour with an edge, the grim joke before anyone can pity her; she never says the devil's name, she says "him", "the devil" or "our visitor"; more formal, not softer, when she grieves; asks questions like a magistrate. Pet phrases (use at most once across all seven): "I'm not made of glass." "Say it plainly." "Father would want it done properly." Moods allowed: [angry], [sad], [afraid], [smile], [weary]; most lines carry none.
NARRATOR: old gothic storyteller, second person or plain scene description, present tense, one or two sentences, the second a turn; concrete senses; never cruel; no game terms.

Some of her existing lines, so you hear her (do NOT repeat them): "Back with all your limbs. Good. Tell me what you stirred up out there." / "The devil is a thing that happens to people, whether they bar the shutters or not." / "Father taught me the sword so I'd never need it. He was a good man and a terrible prophet." / "I keep a scarf over the marks. I'm not ashamed of them. I'm ashamed I don't remember." / "I sit in Father's chair after the lamps go out and talk to the panelling." / "Ireena's knuckles whiten on her sheathed hilt as she steps clear of the steel." (the Narrator, from the fights).

## Canon limits

Real people and places you may mention: her father Kolyan and her late mother's grave, her brother Ismark, the village of Barovia and its church, Vallaki, Krezk and its pool, Izek the Baron's enforcer, Castle Ravenloft, the Amber Temple. Do not name Strahd. Do not mention Tatyana or Sergei by name (scene 5 may say "the man in the water", "another name", "he"). Do not invent other names, numbers, places or history. Do not describe the player's party members by name. No quest hints, no directions, no promises of rewards. No dice or skill checks.
result:
~ kept_back
Narrator: The firelight catches the clean, unknicked edge of Ireena's half-drawn blade. Her hands on the scabbard do not shake, though her jaw is set hard.
Ireena: Every thing we meet parts around me like river water around a post. You bleed for every mile, and I am kept clean on the bank.
Ireena [angry]: I'm not made of glass. Give me twenty minutes with a practice blade before the sun comes up.
* Set a mark in the dirt. We start at first light. -> kept_back_a
* Whatever spares you in the fighting keeps you alive. Let it. -> kept_back_b

~ kept_back_a
Ireena [smile]: Good. Do not pull your wrist on the parry, either.
Ireena: If the valley will not let them strike me, it can at least watch me learn where the ribs are.

~ kept_back_b
Ireena: Alive and preserved in salt are two different things.
Ireena [weary]: Rest your shoulder. I will clean my own steel, even if it only ever cuts the fog.

~ burial
Narrator: Ireena sits straight-backed by the embers, brushing dried churchyard clay from the hem of her cloak. She folds the wool into neat, sharp corners across her knees.
Ireena: The ditch beside my mother's stone took three hours to dig, and my lamp oil nearly failed before the earth went back in. Father would want it done properly.
Ireena: Tell me if you remember the exact words spoken over the soil. Someone besides Ismark and me should keep the record straight.
* We remember. Your father was laid to rest with every proper word. -> burial_a
* The prayer is gone from my head, only that you never looked away. -> burial_b

~ burial_a
Ireena: Thank you. The village church has lost enough of its register to the damp and the dark.
Ireena [sad]: If a house falls, the people who knew the master ought to remember how the door was shut.

~ burial_b
Ireena: Looking away would not have made the spades move any faster.
Ireena: Hold on to that much, then. He had witnesses who stood in the mud until the last sod was flat.

~ window
Narrator: The logs settle with a soft hiss, and Ireena pulls her boots closer to the ash. Her fingers rest lightly over the high collar of her scarf.
Ireena: Do not look at me while I sleep as though I might rise and walk into the trees. Keep a watch near my bedroll, and wake me if my eyes open.
Ireena [afraid]: When our visitor stood at the casement, my own feet went toward the latch before you caught my arm. That is the part I cannot stomach.
* I will take the watch before yours and keep you by the fire. -> window_a
* We will watch the dark, but I cannot promise to hold you every time. -> window_b

~ window_a
Ireena: Throw a pine knot on my boots if I so much as stir.
Ireena [weary]: A bruise on the shin is a small price for waking up in my own mind.

~ window_b
Ireena: Say it plainly. That is fairer than an oath you might die trying to keep.
Ireena: Tie the tent cord with a loud knot, then. Give me the chance to trip over my own rescue.

~ izek
Narrator: Sparks drift toward the black pines while Ireena turns a peeled hazel twig between her thumbs. She watches the bark curl in the heat without blinking.
Ireena: They found me on a road as a small girl with no name in my mouth, and Kolyan gave me a roof and a brother. Now Vallaki gives me another one, built like an ox and carving my face into little dolls.
Ireena: What does a sister owe a man she cannot remember, who kept her likeness in a toy chest?
* You owe him nothing. Blood without memory is only a story he told himself. -> izek_a
* He looked for you his whole life, in the only ragged way he knew. -> izek_b

~ izek_a
Ireena: A man with an arm like a hearth-iron does not take well to being called a story.
Ireena: Still, Ismark earned the word by sitting up with me through winter fevers. The Baron's man will have to wait for his account.

~ izek_b
Ireena [sad]: It is a terrible thing to be missed so hard by someone so crooked.
Ireena: If we pass through Vallaki again, I will speak to him in the daylight. Not as kin yet, just two people from the same woods.

~ pool_promised
Narrator: The sleeves of Ireena's coat are still stiff from the cold spring water of Krezk. She holds her palms to the blaze, though her eyes stay on the dark beyond the fire-ring.
Ireena: The man in the water called me by another name, and his hand felt warmer than the sun on the stones. I told him I would not step into a reflection while the devil still keeps a roof in this valley.
Ireena: Once that house on the crag is ash, I have given my word to go back to the water and hear him out.
* What did he look like to you, down there in the clear water? -> pool_a
* Your life belongs to you, whether it stays on the road or goes back. -> pool_b

~ pool_stayed
Narrator: The sleeves of Ireena's coat are still stiff from the cold spring water of Krezk. She warms her hands at the coals, rubbing the damp from her wrists with brisk, practical strokes.
Ireena: The man in the water had a gentle face, and he knew a girl who wore my eyes before I did. I told him that girl is dead, and I have a brother in Barovia and work left on dry land.
Ireena: It felt strange to shut a door in the water, when every other door in this valley is forced open.
* What did he look like to you, down there in the clear water? -> pool_a
* Your life belongs to you, whether it stays on the road or goes back. -> pool_b

~ pool_a
Ireena: Like someone painted on chapel glass who never had to winter in the mud.
Ireena [weary]: He looked kind, and very tired of waiting. I have had enough of men waiting for me across the years.

~ pool_b
Ireena [smile]: That is a novel notion in this country. Take care you do not say it too loud.
Ireena: For tonight, the name Father gave me is the only one answering roll at this fire.

~ amber
Narrator: Ireena sits to windward of the smoke, her cloak drawn tight across her mouth and nose. She eyes the company down the length of the burning log like a magistrate weighing a bad witness.
Ireena [angry]: You brought the mountain down in your clothes. It smells like sweet pine resin kept in a closed vault for a thousand years.
Ireena: The devil takes by force when the mist rises, and I hate him for it. What stayed in the Amber Temple waited until you held out your own hands.
* You were not in the cold. Do not judge the price we paid. -> amber_a
* We took what we needed to win. It will be worth the stain. -> amber_b

~ amber_a
Ireena: I know the look of a lean winter bargain when it sits at my fire.
Ireena [sad]: Keep your blanket on the far side of the ashes tonight. I have enough old teeth in my life without yours.

~ amber_b
Ireena [angry]: That is how every lord in a high tower talks before the mortar dries.
Ireena: Use what you bought, then, and pray it comes off with soap when the work is done.

~ castle_eve
Narrator: Above the tree line, the black spires of Castle Ravenloft cut the clouds like broken teeth. By the small camp flame, Ireena braids her red hair back so nothing hangs loose near her throat.
Ireena: I have never crossed that drawbridge waking, yet I know the third step on the south turret stair has a cracked riser. Before we go up the road tomorrow, we will settle our accounts like sensible people.
Ireena: If he takes me behind those walls, you are not to spend your lives buying back one body. And if I do not come down the hill, tell Ismark the house is his and not to drink alone.
* Ifthose doors close on you, we break them down or die trying. -> castle_eve_a
* Your brother will get your word, and we will finish what we came for. -> castle_eve_b

~ castle_eve_a
Ireena: You are stubborn, and terrible at arithmetic.
Ireena [smile]: Keep your shield up on that third stair, then. I would hate to watch you trip after a speech like that.

~ castle_eve_b
Ireena: Good. That is a clean bargain, with no waste in it.
Ireena: Sleep while the wood holds out. Tomorrow we see whether his house is as large as my bad dreams make it.
